title: Learning to Predict Future-Aligned Research Proposals with Language Models

paper.authors: Heng Wang, Pengcheng Jiang, Jiashuo Sun, Zhiyi Shi, Haofei Yu, Jiawei Han, Heng Ji (UIUC)
paper.venue: arXiv:2603.27146v3 (26 May 2026); preprint, no venue yet
paper.repo_commit: 59a03f4439df71ef2df5276a3e726cfa1a4e059b (2026-05-08, branch master, single commit 'Initial release'); shallow clone under external/repos/W7148175927/Arthur-Heng__future-aligned-proposals, 237 MB
paper.repo_license: none - no LICENSE file and the GitHub API reports license: null (default all-rights-reserved)
paper.other_artifacts: None. No Hugging Face dataset, no LoRA adapters, and no generated-proposal files are released; data/ ships only the SFT and test inputs.

dependence.note: The paper's whole evaluation signal (Future Alignment Score) is an LLM judgement. The primary judge is GPT-4.1-mini, which is not retiring; the retiring snapshot enters as the high-capability cross-check judge (GPT-5-mini) whose agreement with the primary judge is the evidence that FAS is not an artifact of judge capability. GPT-5 also appears as the reasoning-trace synthesiser for the SFT data (data_synthesis/one_layer_sft.py, reasoning_model default 'gpt-5') - that is a distillation role we do not re-run.

claim.statement: The Future Alignment Score is robust to judge capability: re-scoring the same proposals with GPT-5-mini instead of the primary judge GPT-4.1-mini gives per-example Pearson r = 0.803 / 0.796 / 0.824 and Spearman rho = 0.796 / 0.781 / 0.765 for Stepwise CoT / Untuned / CoI, rates 86.0-89.0% of proposals within 1 point on the 1-10 scale, and recovers the identical model ordering (Table 7, Appendix C).
claim.metric: Per-example Pearson r and Spearman rho between the GPT-5-mini judge's max_llm_score and the GPT-4.1-mini judge's max_llm_score over the same sampled test instances, plus the share of instances whose two scores differ by at most 1 point; and the sign of the induced system ordering.

original_values.ordering_claimed: OURS (Stepwise CoT) > CoI > Untuned on agreement, and OURS > Untuned > CoI on FAS level (Table 6)

claim.original_source: Paper Table 7 (Appendix C, 'Inter-Judge Agreement'); Table 6 gives the n=300 baseline configuration and the FAS levels. The within-1-pt percentages are consistent with n=300 (296/300 = 98.7%, 293/300 = 97.7%, 283/300 = 94.3%, 258/300 = 86.0%), but Table 7 does not restate n.

protocol.model_usage_verified: partly - the paper writes 'GPT-5-mini' with no date and utils/api.py passes the bare alias through to client.chat.completions.create; the repo's own PRICING table in evaluation/validate_robustness.py carries a 'gpt-5-mini' entry at 0.25/2.00, confirming it was actually billed. We pin gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07, the only gpt-5-mini snapshot in harness/pricing.json. Separately, the census live_id 'gpt-4.1-nano' is a reference-list false positive (OpenAI 2025a, 'Introduces GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and GPT-4.1 nano'); the repo does call gpt-4.1-nano, but only to generate summaries and highlight keywords in the human-annotation UI (human_evaluation/serve_comparison.py).
protocol.prompt_source: evaluation/evaluate.py LLM_JUDGE_SUBFIELD_PROMPT (the judge used when --subfield-scores is set, which is the paper's configuration: FAS is reported per component and overall). LLM_JUDGE_PROMPT is the overall-only variant. Paper Appendix E.6 / Figure 12.

messages.content: You are an expert research paper evaluator. [...] ## Generated Proposal: {proposal} ## Candidate Paper: {candidate_summary} ## Task: Rate the similarity on a scale of 0-10 [...] Respond with ONLY a JSON object

params.temperature: NOT SENT for the gpt-5 arm - utils/api.py branches on `if "gpt-5" in model` and omits both temperature and max_tokens, so gpt-5-mini runs at API defaults (default reasoning effort). The gpt-4.1-mini reference judge runs at temperature 0.1 (evaluate.py llm_judge_similarity).
params.max_tokens: not set for gpt-5-mini; not set for gpt-4.1-mini either
params.seed: not set; sampling of test instances uses seed 42 (validate_robustness.py --seed)
params.retrieval: EmbeddingRetriever over text-embedding-3-large, top_k = 10, then the top judge_top_n = 5 retrieved papers are judged; FAS is the max over those 5

protocol.evaluation: evaluation/validate_robustness.py: runs the same 300 sampled predictions per system under two judge configurations, then compute_correlation() (scipy pearsonr / spearmanr) on the per-instance max_llm_score lists, and prints the ranking-consistency check. The within-1-point share is not computed by the shipped script and must be added (a two-line diff on the individual_scores arrays).
protocol.environment: Python >= 3.10, pip install -e . ; OPENAI_API_KEY. A local GPU is needed only to regenerate the proposals (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct / Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct inference at temperature 0.7).

artifacts.prompts_path: evaluation/evaluate.py (LLM_JUDGE_SUBFIELD_PROMPT, LLM_JUDGE_PROMPT, GAP_GROUNDEDNESS_PROMPT); data_synthesis/ holds the structuring and reasoning-synthesis prompts
artifacts.data_path: data/test_set/test_set_n819.jsonl (819 held-out instances, prompts self-contained) and data/test_set/structured_papers.json (12.5 MB future corpus judged against); data/sft/sft_n2823_*.jsonl for training
artifacts.data_license: unstated - no LICENSE in the repo; the underlying content is NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR 2024-2025 paper text structured by GPT-4.1 from OpenReview PDFs
artifacts.notes: The generated proposals (analyze/predictions_819/*.json, the script's default input) are NOT shipped, and neither are the LoRA adapters. validate_robustness.py also defaults to corpus paths data/paper_structured/*.json and data/accepted_papers/*.json that do not exist in the release; the README's data/test_set/structured_papers.json is the shipped equivalent. DEFAULT_CONFIGS contains gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4o-mini and embedding variants but no gpt-5-mini entry - the Table 7 configuration must be added by hand (one RobustnessConfig line).

blockers: The model outputs being judged are not released: reproducing Table 7 requires first regenerating proposals for three systems, and the LoRA adapters are not published.

Regenerating the 'Stepwise CoT' (OURS) system means LoRA-fine-tuning Qwen2.5-14B on data/sft/sft_n2823_stepwise_cot.jsonl, whose reasoning traces were synthesised by gpt-5 (data_synthesis/one_layer_sft.py reasoning_model default). That is training on commercial-model outputs, which this study does not do - so the OURS row is out of scope and only the Untuned and CoI rows can be re-executed.
Judge snapshot named only by alias ('GPT-5-mini'); pinned to gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 by inference.
Table 7 does not state n; we assume the n=300 sample of Table 6 (seed 42). The within-1-point statistic is not implemented in the shipped script.

The GPT-5-mini arm runs at API defaults because utils/api.py strips temperature/max_tokens for gpt-5 models, so reasoning effort is whatever the endpoint defaults to - an uncontrolled parameter that may itself have drifted.
No repository licence; code can be run but not redistributed.

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (P0) - the retiring cross-check judge of Table 7; the gpt-4.1-mini primary judge must be run alongside it because the claim is a correlation between the two

successors: gpt-5.6-terra (vendor-designated replacement for gpt-5-mini per the OpenAI deprecations page)
companion_not_retiring: gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 (primary judge; alive, not on the retirement list - needed as the correlation reference)

budget.assumptions: Restricted variant (Untuned + CoI only, the OURS row excluded as distillation): 2 systems x 300 instances x 5 judge calls x 3 seeds = 9,000 calls per judge, 18,000 total. Input 1,500 tokens per call (the repo's own estimate in validate_robustness.py). Output: gpt-4.1-mini ~60 tokens of JSON; gpt-5-mini assumed ~600 (JSON plus hidden reasoning at default effort, the reasoning-model rule). gpt-5-mini ~USD 14.2, gpt-4.1-mini ~USD 6.3, corpus embeddings ~USD 0.4. One seed instead of three costs ~USD 7. Including the OURS row would add ~50% (USD ~31) on top of the excluded fine-tuning.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Primary numbers: the two per-system Pearson r values for the GPT-5-mini judge (Untuned 0.796, CoI 0.824). Survival = the re-run r for each system lies inside the bootstrap 95% CI over the 300 instances of the original (Fisher-z, about +/- 0.05 at n=300, r ~ 0.8) AND the tool-validity direction holds: agreement stays high (r > 0.7), the within-1-point share stays above 80%, and the GPT-5-mini judge still ranks CoI above Untuned exactly as the GPT-4.1-mini judge does. Partial = r drops below the CI but stays above 0.6 with the ordering intact. Death = the ordering flips under the GPT-5-mini judge, or r falls to a level at which FAS conclusions would depend on judge choice.
judgment.notes: This is a correlation between two judges, so the target moves only if judge behaviour drifts; both judges must be re-run in the same batch, and the proposals must be identical across judges. Because we regenerate the proposals (the originals are not released), the absolute FAS levels of Table 6 are NOT the comparison target - only the judge-agreement statistics, which are a property of the judge pair on comparable material.

user_checks: Accept the restricted target (Untuned + CoI rows of Table 7 only), since regenerating the OURS system would require fine-tuning on gpt-5-synthesised reasoning traces?
Accept regenerating the proposals locally (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct at temperature 0.7 on the 819-item test set, then a 300-item sample at seed 42), given the authors released no predictions?
Pin the alias 'GPT-5-mini' to gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 and run it at API defaults (no temperature, default reasoning effort) as the repo's code does?
Use n=300 (the Table 6 sample) for Table 7, and add the missing within-1-point statistic to validate_robustness.py?
domain_notes: The paper reframes research-proposal generation as time-sliced forecasting: proposals written from pre-2025 inputs are scored by semantic alignment with NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR 2025 papers. The trained systems are open-weight (Qwen2.5-7B/14B, Llama-3.1-8B, LoRA), so the only commercial dependence is the judge, the embedding retriever, the GPT-4.1 paper-structuring step and the GPT-5 reasoning-trace synthesis. Three retiring snapshots appear in the repo in different roles: gpt-5-mini (inspiring-paper selection and the Table 7 judge), gpt-5 (SFT reasoning traces - distillation, excluded) and gpt-4.1-nano (annotator-UI readability summaries - cosmetic). Only the Table 7 judge role has a published number attached to it.
